articles.title: FTC Catches Martin Shkreli Trading 60+ Pharma Stocks Despite Lifetime Ban — Contempt Motion Filed
articles.summary: The FTC and seven states allege that Martin Shkreli — already banned for life from the pharmaceutical industry — continued trading stocks in at least 60 drug companies in blatant defiance of a federal court order. Authorities are now seeking contempt sanctions and forfeiture of all trading profits. This is the pharma industry's favorite scapegoat still gaming the system nobody actually fixed.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid Safety Failures on Its iLet Device — Stock Cratered 37% When Truth Emerged
articles.summary: Beta Bionics allegedly misled investors and patients about the safety, efficacy, and commercial viability of its iLet medical device, triggering a securities fraud class action after shares collapsed more than 37%. The pattern is textbook: safety red flags buried until the market forces disclosure the FDA didn't. Patients using this device deserved that information first.

articles.title: Ensign Group Buried Patient Neglect, Falsified Staffing Data, and Billed Anyway — Securities Fraud Suit Follows
articles.summary: Ensign Group, a major nursing facility operator, faces securities fraud allegations after reports surfaced that it concealed systemic patient neglect, manipulated quality and staffing metrics, engaged in improper billing, and ran an administrator-license rental scheme. The company's stock dropped 8% when the concealment began unraveling. Vulnerable patients paid the real price long before investors did.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces Federal Fraud Complaint — FTC Says Executives Lied to Investors and Patients
articles.summary: Hims & Hers Health and its executives face a securities class action lawsuit filed in the wake of a sweeping FTC federal complaint alleging the company defrauded both investors and patients. The FTC's action suggests systemic misrepresentation at the corporate level, not a rounding error. This is what happens when telehealth moves fast and regulators look the other way.

articles.title: Forced Psychiatric Treatment: Government Asserts It Can Override Your Right to Refuse Medication
articles.summary: A Reason analysis confronts the growing legal and ethical crisis of compelled psychiatric treatment — the premise that a mental illness diagnosis strips a patient of their right to refuse drugs. The question cuts to the core of bodily autonomy and the medical establishment's coercive power. Psychiatry's answer to non-compliance has too often been forced medication, not informed consent.

articles.title: Pancreatic Cancer Cells Continuously Rewrite Their DNA to Outrun Every Drug Thrown at Them
articles.summary: An analysis of nearly half a million cells from dozens of pancreatic cancer patients reveals that tumor cells are in a state of continuous genetic evolution, constantly reshaping their makeup to evade treatment — a finding with massive implications for why standard oncology keeps failing this cancer. The data raises hard questions about why a mutation-chasing drug paradigm consumes billions while survival rates barely move. Follow the cells, not the pharma pipeline.

articles.title: 220 Immunocompromised Patients Got Live Vaccines by Accident — Zero Developed Disease. The Medical Establishment Ignored It.
articles.summary: A study of 220 IBD patients on immunosuppressive biologics who accidentally received live vaccines — including MMR and varicella — showed zero resulting cases of measles, mumps, or chickenpox. This directly challenges the blanket prohibition on live vaccines in immunocompromised patients, a restriction that has left millions unprotected. The data exists. The guidelines haven't moved.

articles.title: Hospital Cartel Sues to Kill Federal Drug Discount Program — $1 Billion a Year Too Transparent for Them
articles.summary: Hospital systems have returned to federal court to block a federal drug-discount rebate program, claiming it would cost them over $1 billion annually to operate — revealing just how profitable the current opaque drug-pricing infrastructure is for provider networks. When hospitals fight transparency this hard, ask what they're protecting. Patients on 340B drugs deserve to know where the money goes.

The question the oncology establishment must answer: how long has this been known, and why hasn't the treatment paradigm shifted?

When the evidence contradicts the dogma, the dogma wins — until it doesn't.

articles.title: GDF15 Deficiency Silently Starves the Fetus — And Nobody Is Talking About What's Suppressing This Protein
articles.summary: New research published in PLOS Biology confirms that placenta-specific GDF15 is essential for fetal growth, with deficiency triggering growth restriction by collapsing the fetal hepatic STAT3-IGF2 signaling axis. Circulating GDF15 levels drop in at-risk pregnancies, yet this biomarker is not part of standard prenatal screening. With miscarriage and fetal growth restriction rates climbing, the failure to act on emerging placental biology is a clinical negligence story hiding in plain sight.

This mechanistic pathway has been largely overlooked by obstetric research priorities dominated by pharmaceutical intervention targets. Understanding what suppresses GDF15 in human pregnancy — including drugs, environmental exposures, and nutritional deficiencies — is a question the system has not been eager to fund.

articles.title: Early-Life Antibiotics Wreck Gut Immunity — Fecal Transplants Show What Drugs Won't Fix

The pediatric overprescription of antibiotics has been documented for decades, yet standard of care has barely changed. This study is further evidence that the microbiome destruction we inflict on children has immunological consequences the pharmaceutical industry has no pill to solve.
